meta.purpose: Cases ordered to lead with joint wins (C3), failure modes (C4) at the end

cases.label: C3 — composition WIN (joint > retrieval on atoms-only KB)
cases.summary: Question composes two atomic concepts: 'cards by Aaron Miller' AND 'incredibly rare'. With composite Formula nodes stripped from the KB, joint still co-fetches both atoms along depends_on edges. Flat-RAG top-5 paraphrases one concept, misses the other. Demonstrates the D3 open-world composition claim.

cases.label: C3 — composition WIN (3-way filter)
cases.summary: Three filters compose: SLE diagnosis + normal hematocrit + oldest patient. Joint atoms-only KB retrieves the three ValueMap atoms via BFS. Retrieval top-5 picks the most-similar bullets and drops one filter. Open-world composition under D3.

cases.label: C4 — retrieval_irrelevance (joint loses)
cases.summary: Question about loan eligibility; joint's top-5 BFS retrieves loan-duration, loan-status, transaction-type — all loan-related but not the eligibility criterion. Failure mode 2 (17/40 audited cases). Shows joint can fetch the wrong neighborhood.

cases.label: C4 — specificity_loss (joint loses)
cases.summary: Question asks about crimes in 1995; oracle has the exact mapping crimes_1995 → A15; joint retrieves a ValueMap pointing at A16 (1996), causing a +1-year error. Failure mode 1 (22/40 cases) — joint lacks question-specific literals oracle supplies.

cases.label: C4 — distraction (joint loses, others get lucky)
cases.summary: Nuanced case: none and retrieval happen to be CORRECT by defaulting to the text column s.DOCType='Unified School District'. Oracle uses the formal DOC code mapping (DOC=54). Joint retrieves irrelevant nodes (Charter School indicator, Fresno Unified value, K-12 grades) that distract the LLM away from the obvious text column. Shows that extra evidence is not always net-positive when retrieval lands on unrelated neighbors.
